issues.body: `test_no_entry_is_reachable_from_a_pr_time_workflow` scans only `_WF_DIR.glob("*.yml")`, and `local_calls` only matches an unquoted `uses: ./.github/workflows/...` value. GitHub Actions also accepts `.yaml` workflow files and quoted scalar values such as `uses: "./.github/workflows/build-matrix.yml"`. A PR-time workflow written in either valid form can call an entry in `_RELEASE_ONLY` without entering `reachable`, so this test remains green while the selector skips Rust jobs for a workflow that now participates in PR CI. That contradicts the stated fail-closed, machine-checked inertness obligation.
issues.fix_hint: Enumerate both `*.yml` and `*.yaml` workflows and parse each workflow's jobs/`uses` values with a YAML-aware implementation, or make the stdlib parser explicitly support optional quoting and both extensions. Add regression fixtures/tests for a quoted local `uses` caller and a PR-triggered `.yaml` caller, each proving the allowlisted callee is detected.
issues.title: Reusable-workflow reachability proof misses valid GitHub Actions syntax

verdict.summary: The current allowlisted workflows appear non-PR-triggered, but the load-bearing reachability test does not establish the durable inertness property claimed by the change. Its caller discovery recognizes only unquoted `uses:` values in `*.yml` files, although GitHub Actions permits quoted values and also supports `*.yaml` workflow files. A future PR-time caller using either valid form would leave an allowlisted reusable workflow classified release-only and could silently skip the Rust lanes it affects.
